scope: Proposition 3.7 (Ring cutoffs) of the manuscript “A Linear Clock for Random Walk on Tree-Weighted Planar Maps” (preprints/A-Linear-Clock-for-Random-Walk-on-Tree-Weighted-Planar-Maps-October-5-2026/linear-clock-random-walk-tree-weighted-planar-maps.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0acb1c84bf79e9c8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a compact subpatch of an ordinary chart and an aspect ratio τ > 1. Along a coupled further extraction from any rate sequence, there is a constant C, depending only on the chart and τ, with the following property. For every fixed disk B(z, τr) contained with a margin in that subpatch, both graphs eventually admit functions χm valued in [0, 1] such that χm = 1 on every lift of B(z, r), χm = 0 on every lift outside B(z, τr), e(χm) ≤ C on the primal graph, with e∗(χm) ≤ C on the dual. Their energy is supported in the indicated ring, up to vanishing projected mesh. The constant is independent of z, r, m; the threshold in m may depend on the fixed disk. These assertions hold simultaneously for the countable buffered disk tests, and extend to arbitrary fixed disks by strict inner and outer margins.
